html:
The Soomras were a local dynasty that ruled Sindh from about the early 11th century to the mid 14th, as the region broke away from distant overlords.

They rose as the Ghaznavids weakened, and for much of their time they paid tribute to stronger powers, later the Delhi Sultanate. Their beliefs are debated: some sources link them to Ismaili Shia Islam, others to Hindu roots. They are remembered above all in Sindhi folklore. The tale of Umar and Marvi, about a Soomra king who carries off a village girl who stays loyal to her home, was sung by the poet Shah Abdul Latif; see Umar Marvi.

Around 1351 power passed to the Sammas. In that same year Muhammad bin Tughluq died near Thatta while campaigning in Sindh.
sum: The Soomras were a local dynasty that ruled Sindh from about the early 11th century to the mid 14th, as the region broke away from distant overlords.
